subject: literature
passage: For thirty years, Mr. Takahashi had locked the greenhouse himself every evening and kept its only key on a cord around his neck. The neighbors' children were allowed to admire his orchids from the doorway but never to touch a watering can. So when Mateus, who had spent the summer quietly sweeping the paths and asking the name of each plant, arrived on Monday, he was surprised to see the old man holding out the cord. "The tall ones need water before noon," Mr. Takahashi said. The passage suggests that Mr. Takahashi ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: had come to trust Mateus with the care of the greenhouse.
choices.B: wanted Mateus to stop asking questions about the plants.
choices.C: planned to sell the greenhouse and its orchids to a neighbor.
choices.D: had always let the neighbors' children water his orchids.

explanation.why: Mr. Takahashi had guarded the greenhouse for thirty years and let no child touch a watering can. Handing his only key to Mateus, along with watering instructions, shows that Mateus's careful summer of work had earned his trust.
explanation.A: Correct. Giving away the only key and explaining when to water show new trust in Mateus.
explanation.B: Incorrect. He answers Mateus with plant-care instructions, which invites more involvement, not less.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text mentions selling the greenhouse.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says children were never allowed to touch a watering can.
